facts.text: Lake St. Croix Beach was one of the last river communities in Washington County to develop, remaining a rural farming area until the early 1900s.
The town site in 1886 consisted of two large farms bisected by the Chicago, Milwaukee & St. Paul Railroad line.
Investors began buying land in the valley in the early 1900s, anticipating a tourism boom fueled by automobile travel from the Twin Cities.
In 1914, the Ford Motor Company reportedly considered the Anchorage site near Lake St. Croix Beach for a factory, but the plant was ultimately built elsewhere.
Unlike neighboring Afton and Lakeland, Lake St. Croix Beach never attracted loggers or commercial development, preserving its rural character.
The city’s name, Lake Saint Croix Beach, reflects its location on the Saint Croix River, a major waterway in Minnesota.
